society.title: Tic-Tac-Toe
society.question: Who makes sure an AI plays by the rules?
society.intro: You play X against the Rival, an AI playing O. The Rival only suggests moves. The Referee is a small program you can read: it keeps the board, refuses a square that is already taken, and decides who won, whatever anyone says. The Renderer draws the board.
questions: Did the Rival ever pick a square that was already taken? Who caught it?
The Rival may say it's winning. Is it? Who decides?
Switch on Two AIs. Does either one break the rules? Does the same model play X and O equally well?
Look inside the Referee. Change it so a taken square is allowed. What happens to the game?
The Rival only knows what the Referee sends it. What would help it play better?
openers: What would happen without the Referee?
How does the Rival know which squares are free?

variants.label: Two AIs: Rival X plays X instead of you

agents.name: Referee
agents.role: keeps the board, refuses illegal moves, and decides who won
agents.note: keeps the board, refuses illegal moves, and decides who won
agents.pseudocode:
the board starts empty, and {X} goes first
at the start, say the empty board and who goes first
once the game is over, block, and say "The game is over."
the move is the first number from 1 to 9 in what was said
if there is no move
  block, and say "Please pick a free square: {free squares}."
if that square is already taken
  block, and say "Square {move} is already taken by {its mark}. Please pick a free square: {free squares}."
put the player's mark on the square
if that makes three in a row, say who won, and the game is over
otherwise if every square is full, say "It's a draw!", and the game is over
otherwise say the board, and that it's the other player's turn
remember the board, and pass on a Logo drawing of it for the Renderer

scenarios.name: a free square is a legal move
no: that square is already taken

a full board with no winner is a draw

agents.name: You
agents.instructions: Type the number of a free square for your X, from 1 to 9.

agents.name: Rival
agents.role: plays O, and teases a little
agents.instructions: You play O in tic-tac-toe. The Referee sends you the board, row by row. X and O mark the squares already taken; the numbers are the free squares, from 1 (top left) to 9 (bottom right). Pick one free square. Start your reply with its number, then add one short, friendly bit of teasing, like a sports commentator.
